commands.author: hugenshen

target.title: security(audit): flag control-plane exposure and plugin command surfaces
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two related gaps in `openclaw security audit` where operators could miss high-impact exposure on open chat surfaces and extension plugin command entry points.

### Gap 1: Control-plane tools on open inbound policy

When a channel uses `groupPolicy="open"` or an open DM policy, the exposure matrix flagged elevated and runtime/filesystem tools but did **not** separately flag **control-plane tools** (`cron`, `gateway`).

### Gap 2: Extension plugin commands on chat command surfaces

The plugin trust audit did not evaluate native command surfaces separately, name affected channels in finding detail, or warn when enabled extension plugins register commands reachable on those surfaces.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Control-plane exposure:** `collectRiskyToolExposureContexts()` now probes `cron` and `gateway`. Emits `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` (critical) when open inbound policy can reach control-plane tools.

**Plugin command surface audit:** `collectPluginsTrustFindings()` adds `collectConfiguredCommandSurfaces()` and new/updated findings:

| checkId | After |
|---|---|
| `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` | critical when native commands **or** skill commands enabled without `plugins.allow`; detail names channels |
| `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` | warn when enabled extensions register commands and native commands are configured |

**Docs:** `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` uses the correct `plugins.allow` config key.

## User Impact

* Operators get clearer findings when open chats can reach gateway/cron control or extension plugin commands.
* `plugins.extensions_no_allowlist` may now report `critical` when native commands are active without `plugins.allow`.
* No runtime behavior change.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts \
  src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Open inbound policy could expose gateway/cron control-plane tools and plugin command surfaces without dedicated audit findings.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin arm64), Node.js v22.22.0, local source checkout on branch `codex/audit-plugin-command-control-surface` (single commit on latest `main`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/security/audit-plugins-trust.test.ts src/security/audit-trust-model.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ security audit trust model findings > evaluates trust-model exposure findings
   (includes security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane scenarios)
 ✓ security audit install metadata findings > evaluates install metadata findings
   (includes plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface scenarios)

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Production collectors `collectExposureMatrixFindings` and `collectPluginsTrustFindings` emit `security.exposure.open_groups_with_control_plane` for open group + coding profile setups and `plugins.commands_reachable_chat_surface` when enabled extensions register commands on configured native command surfaces.
- **What was not tested:** Full `openclaw security audit --deep` CLI against a live gateway; no committed `scripts/proof-*.mjs` helpers. Control-plane check ID overlaps with [#100965](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100965) — maintainers should pick one canonical contract.

## AI-assisted disclosure

- AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- Human-directed scope and review of audit logic
